text: Miss World 1958 was the eighth edition of the Miss World pageant, held at the Lyceum Ballroom in London, United Kingdom, on 13 October 1958. Charles Eade and Bob Russell crowned Penelope Coelen of South Africa as Miss World 1958, marking South Africa's first victory and Africa's second win in the pageant's history. Twenty contestants participated in the event, with one contestant appointed to represent her country after contracting an illness from the previous edition. The pageant was hosted by Bob Russell. Miss Belgium 1958, Michele Gouthals, was scheduled to compete but did not participate because her organization appointed Miss Belgium 1957, Jeanne Chandelle, to represent Belgium again, as she had contracted the Asian Flu during the Miss World 1957 pageant and only attended the coronation day. This edition featured the debut of Brazil, and the returns of Turkey, which last competed in 1953, and Norway, which last competed in 1954. Hanni Ehrenstrasser of Austria withdrew after winning Miss Europe 1958, making her ineligible for Miss World; Elisabeth Schubel-Auer was set to replace her but did not proceed for undisclosed reasons. Leila Saas of Egypt, Pirkko Mannola of Finland, Hjördís Sigurvinsdóttir of Iceland, Lydie Schmit of Luxembourg, and Denise Orlando of Tunisia also withdrew for undisclosed reasons. Australia withdrew after failing to hold a national competition or appoint a candidate. Janet Ohene-Agyei Boateng of Ghana withdrew due to financial constraints, and Krystyna Żyła of Poland was barred by her government from competing; she was eventually found dead in December 1958. The number of placements was reduced from seven to six in this edition, with the six finalists selected through a preliminary competition on the day of the final, consisting of a swimsuit and an evening gown segment. Twenty contestants competed for the title.
